originalTitle: Iran's president tells Trump it will never 'bend the knee'
title: Two Big Leaders Talk About Peace!
content:
Hello, amazing young friends! Your friendly African news reporter is here to tell you about some important grown-up news from far away. Sometimes, big leaders from different countries talk to each other about very important things. Today, we are going to learn about two of these big leaders and what they said. It's a bit like when friends need to talk things out, but on a much, much bigger scale for the whole world!

What Happened Far Away?

Imagine two very important grown-ups, like a principal from one school and a principal from another school, who have a big disagreement. Well, this is happening between two countries. One country is called Iran, and its leader is President Pezeshkian. The other country is called the USA, and its leader is President Trump. President Trump, the leader from the USA, said some very strong words. He said that if a 'peace deal' is not made soon, he might 'annihilate' Iran. That's a really big and serious word, isn't it? 'Annihilate' means to completely destroy something, to make it disappear, like when you build a tall, tall sandcastle at the beach and then a big wave comes and washes it all away. Poof! Gone. Now, what is a 'peace deal'? Think of it like this: when you and your friend have an argument, and then you both say sorry and promise to be kind and play nicely again. That promise is like a peace deal. It's an agreement to stop fighting or arguing and find a way to be friends or at least get along. So, President Trump was saying that a peace deal needed to happen quickly.

President Pezeshkian's Strong Reply

When President Pezeshkian from Iran heard these very strong words from President Trump, he also gave a strong answer! He said that Iran would 'never bend the knee'. This is an old saying, and it means that they would never give up, never surrender, and never say 'you win' to someone else. It's like when you're playing a game, and you’re trying your very best. Even if it's hard, you don't just stop and say 'I give up'. You keep going! So, President Pezeshkian said his country would stand strong and not give in. He spoke these powerful words at a very special place where all the world's leaders meet. It's called the United Nations, or UN for short. It's a place where grown-up leaders from almost every country in the world come together to talk about big problems.

What is the United Nations (UN)?

Did you know there's a giant meeting hall for the whole world? It’s true! It's called the United Nations, and it's like a really, really big school assembly, but for leaders of countries! Leaders travel from all corners of the globe to go there. They sit and talk about how to make the world a better, safer place for everyone. Their main job is to try and help countries be friends, or at least talk nicely, instead of fighting. They talk about big problems like how to help people who are hungry, how to keep everyone safe, and how to protect our Earth. President Pezeshkian stood on a special stage at the UN to share his country’s message with all the other world leaders. **Did you know?** The United Nations was created a long, long time ago after a very big war, because countries wanted to find a better way to solve their problems without fighting again. It helps countries talk instead of shout!

Why Are They Talking So Strongly?

This big talk between the leaders is about some very old and serious disagreements that their countries have had for a long, long time. It's not like a small argument about who gets to play with a toy. These are big grown-up problems about rules, safety, and what each country thinks is fair. Both leaders believe they are doing what is best to protect their own people and their homes. They want to make sure their country is strong and safe. Sometimes, when people have very different ideas, they might use strong words to show how serious they are. It’s a way of saying, 'This is very important to us!' It’s like when you really, really want to tell your parent something important, and you use your biggest voice.

What Does 'Peace' Mean for Everyone?

Peace is a beautiful word, isn't it? It means being calm, being safe, and not having any fighting or arguments. When there is peace, children can go to school, play with their friends, learn new things, and just be happy without any worries. A 'peace deal' is like a promise between countries that they will stop arguing and try to work together, so everyone can live in peace. **Did you know?** Many people all over the world, including here in Africa, wish for peace every single day. We all hope that leaders will choose to talk and find solutions that bring peace, because peace is good for everyone. It helps families grow, communities thrive, and children play freely.

Why is This Important for Us?

Even though Iran and the USA are countries far away from our homes here in Africa, what happens in the world can sometimes affect everyone. When big countries have disagreements, it can make other countries worried too. It's like when two very big elephants argue in the forest; all the smaller animals pay attention. But when countries talk, even with strong words, it's always better than fighting. It means they are trying to find a way to sort things out. Our biggest hope is always that leaders will find a way to make a 'peace deal'. It shows us that while it's good to be brave and strong, it's even better to be smart and wise and try to find a peaceful way to solve problems, just like we learn at school and at home. **Did you know?** Our African continent has many different countries, and our own leaders also meet often to talk about how to keep peace and help all our people grow strong and happy! Everyone wants a world where kids can play without fear.

Let's Hope for Peace!

So, we learned about President Pezeshkian from Iran and President Trump from the USA. They used some very strong words, one talking about 'annihilate' and the other saying 'never bend the knee'. But the most important thing is that they were talking at the United Nations, a special place for peace talks and finding solutions. Let’s all hope that these big grown-ups, these important leaders, can keep talking things through. Let’s hope they find a way to make a great 'peace deal' that makes everyone safe and happy. Because peace is the very best thing for all children, everywhere in the world! Keep shining bright, young friends! Your African news reporter hopes for a peaceful world for all of us!
summary: Leaders from Iran and the USA are using strong words while talking about making a peace agreement, with one saying they won't give up and the other threatening big action if a deal isn't reached soon.
whyMatters: It's important because when big countries talk about serious problems, it can affect many people around the world, and everyone hopes that leaders can find a peaceful way to solve their disagreements.
